query: How does resolution duration vary across incident category and priority?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Directly categorizes incidents from short_description, giving a clean grouping axis the query explicitly needs. Values (connectivity, vpn_access, database, printing) are sound readings of the source text. Some redundancy with the existing 'category' column, but the derived taxonomy from text is finer-grained and useful.

per_column.name: resolution_complexity
per_column.rationale: A reassigned-vs-single_assignment axis is analytically relevant to resolution duration. However, the evidence samples expose only short_description/opened_at/closed_by, none of which record reassignment history. Whether an incident was reassigned is not derivable from the shown source text, so the specific values appear asserted rather than grounded.

per_column.name: incident_severity_signal
per_column.rationale: A severity/scope axis pairs well with the duration/priority query. Some values are warranted readings (connectivity_interruption, access_denial), but distinctions like 'server_outage_level', 'multi_system_impact', or 'single_system' vs 'user_workstation' imply scope details the terse descriptions do not clearly state, so groundedness is partial.

per_column.name: incident_repeat_pattern
per_column.rationale: Recurring-vs-isolated could add leverage, but it is not derivable from a single row's source text; identifying recurrence needs cross-row/history evidence not shown. Two nearly identical VPN descriptions get different labels (isolated vs recurring), indicating the value is largely invented rather than grounded.

per_column.name: affected_service_domain
per_column.rationale: A reasonable domain grouping derivable from the description, but it is largely a coarser restatement of incident_category (email->communication_platform, database->data_platform), giving limited new analytical leverage. Values are well grounded, though the VPN->identity_access mapping is debatable.

judge.rationale: The set provides several genuine grouping axes (category, service domain, severity) relevant to analyzing resolution duration by category/priority. However, three columns (resolution_complexity, incident_repeat_pattern, and parts of incident_severity_signal) assert properties—reassignment history, recurrence, system scope—that the exposed source text does not support, with a clear contradiction in the repeat_pattern labeling of near-identical VPN rows. incident_category is strong and well grounded; affected_service_domain is grounded but partly redundant.
